name: Angela Bennett
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Angela Bennett's wellspring of wealth is her share of a royalty paid by mining giant Rio Tinto on every ton of iron ore it mines in Western Australia.
The royalty was negotiated by her father, Peter Wright, and his partner, Lang Hancock, father of fellow Australian billionaire Gina Rinehart.
Bennett holds a major stake in Wright Prospecting, which is in litigation with Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting over various iron-ore properties.
In December 2025 she sold a 15% stake in the Rhodes Ridge iron ore project in western Australia to Japanese giant Mitshui & Co in a $2 billion deal.
Bennett's son Todd Bennett is the executive director of her private investment company AMB Holdings.

name: Howard Schultz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Howard Schultz took charge of Starbucks in the 1980s and turned a regional coffee company into one of the world's top brands.
Schultz expanded Starbucks from 11 stores to more than 35,000 worldwide and made it a social hub for many Americans.
He served three stints as CEO, most recently stepping down in early 2023.
Schultz explored a 2020 presidential bid, but said in September 2019 that he would not run because it would risk the re-election of Donald Trump.
His Schultz Family Foundation invests in training and hiring veterans and youths, helping veterans ensure a smooth transition back into civilian life.
Through his VC firm Maveron Capital, Schultz invests in other consumer businesses such as Groupon, Madison Reed, Allbirds and Lucy.
forbes_facts: Schultz grew up in a Brooklyn housing project. When he was 7, his dad, a cloth diaper delivery driver, fell on the job; he had no insurance or salary.
The first person in his family to graduate from college, Schultz attended Northern Michigan University on a football scholarship.

name: Warren Stephens
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Warren Stephens is an investing billionaire and the current United State ambassador to the United Kingdom.
His uncle Witt founded Little Rock-based investment bank Stephens Inc. in 1933; his father Jackson joined in 1946.
The outfit underwrote Walmart's public offering in 1970.
The two brothers plowed their earnings into private equity, hewing to the investment criteria, "whim and caprice."
Stephens grew up in the business, became CEO in 1986 and bought out his cousins in 2006.
Stephens sold a group of newspaper holdings, including the Las Vegas Review Journal, for $400 million in 2015.
forbes_facts: A golf nut, Stephens built the Alotian Club outside Little Rock; it's ranked one of the nation's best.

name: Matteo Danieli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Matteo Danieli cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Luca Ferrari, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Richard Chandler
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: A native of New Zealand, Richard Chandler relocated to Singapore in 2006 where he now runs global investment firm Clermont Group.
Clermont's portfolio includes interests in healthcare, financial services and aerospace.
Clermont has stakes in SBFC, an Indian provider of small business loans, and Hoan My, a healthcare group in Vietnam.
Clermont owns magniX, which develops advanced batteries, energy-storage systems and electric powertrains for aircraft.
forbes_facts: Chandler previously cofounded investment firm Sovereign Global with his brother, Christopher, who now runs his own Legatum Group in Dubai.
In 2021, MagniX won a $74 million, five-year contract from NASA to support its research in electrified aircraft propulsion.

name: Harindarpal Banga
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2025)
forbes_bio: Originally from Chandigarh, India, Harindarpal Banga, known as Harry, has lived in Hong Kong since the 1970s.
The former vice-chairman of Noble Group made his fortune over a 21-year career with one of Asia's largest commodity traders.
He cashed in the last of his Noble shares in 2012, and started Hong Kong-based Caravel Group with sons Guneet and Angad in 2013.
Caravel Group trades and ships commodities.
Banga was an early investor and still holds a stake in India's online beauty retailer Nykaa, which went public in Mumbai in 2021.
forbes_facts: In 2018 the National Maritime Day Celebrations Committee and the Directorate General of Shipping, India, honored him with the NMD Award of Excellence.

name: Christina Rohde
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Christina Rohde is the largest shareholder of German technology company, Rohde & Schwarz.
The business, which has annual revenue of more than 3 billion euros, was founded in 1933 by Lothar Rohde and Hermann Schwarz, and is still controlled by heirs from both families.
The company's first product was a portable crystal clock. It now makes equipment for a range of industries, including air travel, broadcasting and security.
The family-owned company has paid dividends totaling more than 2.3 billion euros to its shareholders since 2006.

name: Jimmy John Liautaud
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Jimmy John Liautaud is the founder of sandwich chain Jimmy John's.
He launched the business in 1983 using a $25,000 loan from his father, an army veteran.
As a student, Liautaud had struggled with undiagnosed dyslexia and graduated second-to-last in his high school class.
Jimmy John's now has 2,800 locations; virtually all of them are franchises.
Liautaud merged his stake in Jimmy John's into Inspire Brands in 2019.
forbes_facts: Liautaud owns dozens of luxury cars, including numerous Ferraris and Porsches.
His three children are all certified to serve as managers of Jimmy John's restaurants.

name: Bris Rocher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Bris Rocher became the CEO of French cosmetics giant Groupe Rocher at the age of 31, after the death of his grandfather and the company's founder Yves Rocher.
Groupe Rocher owns beauty and personal care brands such as Yves Rocher, Arbonne, and Dr. Pierre Ricaud, as well as the French clothing line Petit Bateau.
In July 2023, Bris stepped down as chief executive of Groupe Rocher, delegating the position to non-family member Jean-David Schwartz. He remains chairman of the company.
Along with his uncle Daniel, Bris is one of the largest shareholders of Groupe Rocher, which remains under family control; the company brought in approximately 2.4 billion euros in sales in 2022.

name: Joe Lacob
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Joe Lacob led an ownership group that in 2010 paid $450 million for the Golden State Warriors NBA team.
The value of the team is nearly 15 times more since then, and his 25% stake is worth nearly $2 billion, net of debt.
The Warriors have won four titles since 2010, and posted the best record in NBA history during the 2015-16 season, with 73 wins.
Lacob was a minority owner of the NBA's Boston Celtics for five years before selling to buy the Warriors.
Lacob joined venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins in 1987 and led investments in over 50 startup companies; he is no longer with the firm.

name: Matthew Roszak
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Matthew Roszak is a cryptocurrency investor and cofounder and chairman of Bloq, a blockchain startup that consults on projects such as helping banks store digital assets.
Bloq also helps companies that are trying to process transactions for "stablecoins," or cryptocurrencies pegged to the value of a fiat currency.
In the 1990s and early 2000s, Roszak worked in venture capital and as an entrepreneur before amassing a crypto portfolio starting in 2012.
He settled insider trading charges in 2006 related to stock purchases of Blue Rhino, a propane tank exchange business.
Roszak co-led an initiative to give each member of Congress $50 worth of digital assets; some accepted, but not all.

name: Jerry Moyes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Jerry Moyes and his father founded Swift Transportation in 1966 with one truck, moving cotton and imported steel between Arizona and California
Swift grew to nearly 20,000 trucks and some $4 billion in annual revenue before it merged with Knight Transportation in 2017.
Moyes sold much of his stake in Knight-Swift prior to 2022. Now concentrates on SME Industries, a steel fabricator and construction company in Utah.
Moyes owned the Phoenix Coyotes hockey team, with minority partner Wayne Gretzky, until the team filed for bankruptcy in 2009 and was sold to the NHL.
forbes_facts: Moyes resigned as Swift CEO in 2005 after an insider-trading case (he did not admit to wrongdoing). Two years later, he took Swift private in a leveraged buyout.
Moyes took Swift public once again in 2010, listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

name: Bryan Glazer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Bryan Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $5.2 billion (net of debt).
Bryan co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Joel and Edward. Joel co-chairs Man U with brother Avram. Another brother, Kevin, runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is chairman of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and two other family charitable foundations.

name: Rosely Schweizer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2014-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Rosely Schweizer owns 12.5% of Dr. August Oetker, a $9 billion (sales) conglomerate with interests in food, beverages, chemicals and hotels.
The business began in 1891 when her great-grandfather, pharmacist August Oetker, started selling non-perishable baking powder.
After World War II, her father, former Nazi SS officer Rudolf August Oetker, developed additional food products and successfully diversified.
Rosely studied economics in Innsbruck, Austria, and worked at the family's sparkling wine and spirits company, Henkell & Soehnlein.
Rosely, who has been active in politics with Germany's Christian Democratic Union, served as the parent company's advisory board chairwoman until 2010.
forbes_facts: In 2001, Rosely Schweizer joined with the German Society of Female Entrepreneurs to found the Kaete-Ahlmann-Foundation, named after her grandmother.
In 2019, her son Rudolf Louis Schweizer became chairman of Dr. August Oetker's board.
